review_candidates.title: Head of On-Premise Computing
review_candidates.description: A Snapshot of Your Day As Head of On-Premise Computing, you lead Siemens Energy's global data-center and industrial-edge platforms, ensuring reliable, secure, resilient, and cost-transparent compute, storage, virtualization, private-cloud, and data-protection services. You translate infrastructure strategy into a prioritized roadmap, drive standardized operations and lifecycle management, and enable sites, factories, and applications to consume secure on-premise services through automation, governance, and product-based service delivery. Working across infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, and business stakeholders, you balance reliability, risk, cost, and modernization while reducing technology risk and strengthening operational resilience. How You’ll Make An Impact Customer and Site Focus: Treat infrastructure consumers and sites as customers, translate local production and application demand into supported platform choices, remove adoption friction, and align changes with business-critical windows. Global Platform Leadership: Lead the global On-Premise Computing team, set clear objectives, allocate capacity, develop technical and service leadership, build succession, and create one team culture across central teams, local contributors, employees, and partners. Platform-as-a-Product: Own the team roadmap and lifecycle for standardized compute, virtualization and private cloud, storage, data protection, approved container and bare-metal services. Publish service tiers, catalogues, APIs, and golden paths while managing adoption, quality, technical debt, and retirement. Reliable Day-2 Operations: Ensure observability, incident and problem response, change and configuration control, capacity, patching, backup and recovery, continuity, operational documentation, and L2/L3 engineering are effective across the assigned estate. Estate Visibility and Lifecycle: Maintain trustworthy discovery, inventory, and CMDB records; track supportability across hardware, firmware, hypervisors, operating platforms, and storage; and manage refresh, end-of-life, warranties, licenses, spares, and secure decommissioning. Industrial Edge Standardization: Define and implement approved edge service tiers and reference patterns for compute, storage, virtualization, remote management, local resilience, and site-to-core or cloud integration without assuming ownership of OT applications or control systems. Modernization and Consolidation: Identify obsolete, duplicate, or uneconomic environments; shape approved migration, modernization, and closure waves; coordinate cutover and stabilization; and complete technical and asset decommissioning with application, site, Cloud, and service owners. Capacity, Facilities and Sustainability: Forecast compute, storage, rack, power, and cooling demand; provide technical requirements to site and facility owners; identify constraints; improve utilization and energy transparency; and embed sustainable, circular lifecycle practices in platform decisions. Security, Compliance and Cyber Resilience: Implement approved hardening, privileged access, vulnerability remediation, immutable data protection, and cyber-recovery controls. Maintain evidence, test recovery, and escalate material policy or risk exceptions to authorized owners. Providers and Commercial Outcomes: Integrate hardware vendors, colocation providers, managed-service partners, field services, and local support into one operating model. Monitor service, financial, and lifecycle outcomes, enforce knowledge transfer, and retain internal competence. Executive Communication and Performance Transparency: Translate complex operational, technical, financial, and lifecycle topics into clear insights for senior stakeholders and report outcome-based performance across service health, risk, capacity, cost, sustainability, and improvement. AI Enablement AI-Ready Industrial Edge Foundations: Provide governed base infrastructure for approved low-latency inference, local data processing, and industrial-edge workloads, including fit-for-purpose compute, storage, resilience, remote management, observability, and lifecycle capabilities. Workload Placement Collaboration: Coordinate placement and technical requirements with Cloud, Data, AI, and HPC/GECOT teams, ensuring workloads are directed to the industrial edge, central data center, specialist platform, or public cloud through the approved enterprise decision framework. AIOps and Intelligent Automation: Automate provisioning, configuration, compliance, patching, observability, and recovery using reusable patterns and remote orchestration. Coordinate cross-domain platforms and agent lifecycle standards with Infrastructure Automation & AI Operations while owning implementation and outcomes in the on-premises domain. Responsible Operational Adoption: Introduce AI-assisted monitoring, predictive insight, decision support, and approved automated remediation within established operational, security, risk, and change governance, with clear human accountability and measurable service outcomes. AI Infrastructure Boundaries: Enable shared infrastructure foundations without assuming ownership of enterprise AI strategy, models, use cases, data products, OT applications, or the specialist HPC/GECOT platform. What You Bring Infrastructure Leadership Experience: Typically 10+ years across enterprise data centers, compute, storage, virtualization or private cloud, infrastructure platforms, edge computing, or production operations, including substantial people-leadership responsibility in a distributed or international environment. Platform and Data-Center Expertise: Strong technical judgment across enterprise servers and bare metal, virtualization and hyperconverged platforms, storage, backup and recovery, approved container platforms, operating systems, remote management, colocation, and data-center operations. Industrial and Edge Experience: Practical experience with industrial sites, plants, or other distributed mission-critical locations, including IT/OT boundaries, production change windows, local resilience, and constrained remote support. Transformation Delivery: A track record delivering complex estate consolidation, migration, hardware and platform refresh, end-of-life remediation, data-center transition, or decommissioning programs with measurable closure. Operations, Automation and Cyber Recovery: Strong knowledge of observability, SRE practices, ITSM and CMDB, configuration management, infrastructure-as-code, automation, patching, vulnerability remediation, and cyber recovery. Facilities and Sustainability Understanding: Working knowledge of power, cooling, rack density, physical security, and facility resilience sufficient to define technology requirements and manage dependencies with site and facility specialists. Capacity and Commercial Management: Practical command of capacity planning, lifecycle economics, capital and operating forecasts, asset and license management, colocation and hardware commercial models, and vendor performance. AI and Workload Placement Judgment: Understanding of infrastructure for edge AI, local data processing, and HPC-adjacent requirements, with sound judgment on appropriate placement across edge, central data center, specialist platform, and public cloud. Product and Service Mindset: Ability to turn stakeholder demand into service tiers, a coherent roadmap, golden paths, service objectives, lifecycle decisions, and an evidence-based improvement backlog. Stakeholder Leadership: Excellent collaboration across sites, application teams, OT, Facilities, Cloud, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Network, Finance, and senior infrastructure leadership, with the ability to influence without relying on hierarchy. Qualifications: Degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Relevant data-center, private-cloud, virtualization, storage, security, service-management, FinOps, or sustainability certifications are advantageous. Languages: Fluent English is required. Additional languages are advantageous. About The Team You will be part of Digital Core Infrastructure at Siemens Energy and lead a global, distributed team responsible for shared on-premises computing platforms across global and regional data centers, colocation facilities, site and factory data centers, server rooms, and approved industrial-edge locations. The team operates a centrally governed, federated delivery model, combining global platform architecture, engineering, lifecycle, and service accountability with regional and local demand context, production coordination, and approved operational support. The team works closely with Cloud Computing to shape hybrid patterns and workload placement, with sites and factories to protect local production outcomes, with the Operations Control Center for cross-domain operational command, and with Infrastructure Automation & AI Operations to implement reusable automation and AI-enabled operational capabilities. Together, these partnerships create standardized, resilient, supportable, and future-ready infrastructure from core data centers to the industrial edge. Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo Our Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical Jobs & Careers
